A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same survey. All 12 pages of v1 and 15 pages of v2, including figures, tables, mathematical content and references, support comparison. Neither PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: V1 summarizes methods and findings attributed to earlier studies. It reports no original experiments, simulations, user studies or empirical data analyses.

after.justification: V2's new Tables 5 and 7 explicitly compile existing results from cited studies. Its business statistics are also externally attributed; no original empirical evaluation is reported.

M1.justification: The survey taxonomy and reviewed algorithm descriptions are retained. The added task formulations define background problems without introducing a new algorithm, architecture or training objective.

E1.justification: Neither version reports training or evaluation conducted for this survey. V2's dataset catalog adds descriptive coverage, including BIGPATENT, DeepPatent2 and HUPD, without using them in new experiments.

E2.justification: The studies in v1's method-summary Tables 2–4 are retained in v2's Tables 4, 6 and 8. The new score tables report these studies' findings without introducing an evaluated comparator set against a proposed method.

E3.justification: No new or revised evaluation protocol is reported. The added tables document existing studies' metrics and classification levels without establishing changes to splits, preprocessing, training budgets or testing procedures.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, robustness tests, error analyses or evaluated case studies. V2's business-tool examples and task challenges are descriptive discussion rather than additional empirical analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. V2's new result tables contain point scores and dataset-specific pairs, without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial numerical summaries of previously discussed studies in Tables 5 and 7, absent from v1. Examples include Grawe et al.'s classification accuracy of 0.63 and F1 of 0.62, and Kang et al.'s retrieval F1 of 81.48. These are newly included published results, not demonstrated performance improvements between versions.

T1.justification: V1 describes tasks verbally; v2's Section 2.1 adds mathematical formulations for binary multi-label targets, similarity-ranked retrieval and parameterized generation. These are limited additions of formal task definitions; neither version contains theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a survey of more than 40 papers from 2017–2023, covering text and images through a novel taxonomy of patent tasks and AI methods. The revised audience wording does not change these central contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds qualifications concerning section selection, prompting, low-quality sketches, sparse design-patent text, hallucination and human oversight in Sections 2.1 and 4.1–4.2. These extend the existing limitations and future directions while retaining the main interpretations.

D1.justification: New Section 2.2 and Table 3 provide seven datasets' sizes, formats, modalities and intended tasks, plus bulk-download sources. Section 3.2.3 also removes the statement that Kang et al.'s BERT was used 'without fine-tuning'; this removes a disclosed detail without establishing a changed procedure.

R1.justification: V2 retains the earlier references and adds seven entries covering dataset resources and commercial tools, including DeepPatent2, BIGPATENT, HUPD, Qatent, DaVinci and Questel. This extends practical coverage while preserving the survey's positioning relative to earlier research.

P1.justification: V2 subdivides the task descriptions, adds formulation and challenge paragraphs, introduces Section 2.2 and business discussion, and merges the two multimodal future-direction subsections. The abstract and surrounding prose receive local edits; the main method-review narrative remains largely unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands the tabular presentation with a CPC hierarchy example, a dataset catalog and separate classification and retrieval score tables. The original four tables are retained and renumbered or relocated, and both figures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2's dataset guidance, accessible summaries of published scores and explicit failure conditions make the survey more useful and better qualified than v1. The gains are limited by unexplained mixed mAP scales in Table 7 and Section 4.2's unsupported new assurance that up-to-date patent data prevents replication of existing inventions.
